Published online:
    September 4, 2026

Geographic focus:
    Global (primary focus: US, with notable coverage of Japan, China, South Korea, Europe)

Temporal focus:
    T1. Historical report [YES] — References prior bond rout, previous payrolls miss (-23k), past intervention levels
    T2. Forward-looking reporting short-term risks (next few weeks/months) [YES] — September FOMC meeting, August payrolls release, BOJ September/October meeting, Strait of Hormuz/oil risk
    T3. Forward-looking reporting long-term risks (next quarters/years) [NO]

Synopsis:
    Fed Governor Waller struck a dovish pivot, signaling willingness to hold rates steady at the September FOMC meeting if disinflation data continues to print. This directly cooled rate-hike odds (63% → 50%), sparked a Treasury rally (bull steepening, short-end led), weakened the USD (-0.6% overnight, DXY ~99), and turbocharged JPY strength (+2.3% weekly). Risk assets responded positively — Asian equities broadly rallied, NQ/ES futures are up. Key near-term catalyst remains the August NFP (consensus: +56k vs prior -23k). Lingering tail risks include sticky services inflation (prices paid at 3-year high), elevated long-end yields (30Y at 5.237%), oil near 6-week highs ($95.52 Brent), and unresolved Iran/Strait of Hormuz geopolitical tension. JPMorgan flags that Chair Warsh remains the hawkish wildcard — if he advocates for a hike, one likely follows.

Q01. Is the content relevant to US economy, US yields, US interest rates and US market pricing?
Relevance: YES — Directly covers Fed rate expectations, Treasury yield moves, USD, NFP, services inflation, and futures pricing across ES/NQ

Q02. Is the content about increasing US interest rates?
Relevance: 45 (Residual hike risk remains — 50% market-implied probability for September, Warsh hawkish wildcard, services inflation at 3-year high)
Increasing rates magnitude: ~25bps (standard single hike increment implied by market pricing)

Q03. Is the content about holding stable US interest rates?
Relevance: 60 (Waller explicitly favors holding; the dovish shift is the dominant fresh narrative; data-dependent majority bar for hiking described as "elevated")

Q04. Is the content about decreasing US interest rates?
Relevance: 10 (No serious discussion of cuts; bond rally is relief from hike fears, not cut anticipation)
Decreasing rates magnitude: N/A

Q05. Focus on the very latest information: Is it striking a different sentiment/tone compared to previous discussions on US interest rates?
Difference: -55 (Meaningfully more dovish than before — Waller's hold signal and disinflation acknowledgment directly reverses the recent hawkish narrative driven by the global bond rout and Warsh's prior comments)

Q06. Focus on the very latest information: How does it compare to previous information on US interest rates?
Difference: -55 (Prior sessions were pricing ~63% hike probability amid a global bond selloff and Warsh's hawkish lean; Waller's intervention marks a clear dovish step-change, pulling market pricing back and validating the hold camp, though Warsh's influence keeps the shift from being a full dovish capitulation)
